cards.text: Jesus is up on the mountain, teaching His disciples (Matthew 5:1-2). He just told them to give, pray and fast in secret, and their Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward them (Matthew 6:1-18). Now He says, 'Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth,' and friend, I'm already leaning in.

cards.question: Jesus says not to store up treasures on earth. What's the problem with treasure kept down here?

answers.text: Moth and rust destroy it and thieves steal it
Tax collectors come and take half of it
Kings seize it to pay their armies

cards.text: So Jesus says to store up treasures in heaven instead, where moth and rust do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal. Friend, I went dull in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS, so a place with no rust sounds like a vacation to me.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says your heart ends up wherever your treasure is.

cards.text: Then Jesus changes the picture and says the eye is the lamp of the body. If your eyes are good, your whole body will be full of light.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says bad eyes leave only part of the body in darkness.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, 'If then the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!' That's like the power going out, you grab the flashlight, click it on, and NOTHING, friend, because the one thing that was supposed to light the way is dark too.
Ever had two managers text you opposite orders at the exact same time, friend? Jesus says no one can serve two masters.

cards.question: Jesus says no one can serve two masters. What does He say happens to the one who tries?

answers.text: He'll love one and hate the other
He'll get worn out by both of them
He'll end up working for neither

cards.question: Then Jesus lands it, right after all that talk about treasure: you cannot serve both God and ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, 'Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear.' Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer flinching every time somebody dug in there for scissors, so this one's for me.

cards.question: Right after saying don't worry, Jesus asks a question about food and clothes. What's His point?

answers.text: Life and body are worth more than food and clothes
Food and clothes are a waste of money
Fasting matters more than eating ever will

cards.text: Then Jesus says to look at the birds of the air: they do not sow or reap or gather into barns. Not ONE bird out there has a retirement plan, friend.

cards.question: The birds don't sow, reap or gather into barns. So how does Jesus say they eat?

answers.text: They take from the farmers' barns
They fly to wherever fields are full

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the birds are worth more than you are.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, 'Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?' Friend, I worried in that drawer for years, and the only thing it ever added was dust.
Then He turns to clothes: 'Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.' Those flowers never sewed a single stitch, and they STILL show up dressed for a wedding.

cards.question: Jesus brings up Solomon, the king of Israel who outdid every king on earth in riches (1 Kings 10:23). True or false: Jesus says Solomon in all his glory was dressed better than one of these lilies.

cards.text: Here's the thing about those flowers: they're grass of the field, here today, and tomorrow thrown into the furnace. Gorgeous. And gone.

cards.question: If that's how God clothes the grass that's gone tomorrow, Jesus asks, will He not much more ___ you?

cards.text: Then Jesus calls them, 'O you of little faith,' and tells them not to worry, saying, 'What shall we eat?' or 'What shall we drink?' or 'What shall we wear?' That's the whole worry list, friend, and He just took the pen away.

cards.question: Jesus says the Gentiles strive after food, drink and clothes. What does He say your heavenly Father knows?
Instead of chasing food, drink and clothes, what does Jesus say to seek first?

answers.text: The kingdom of God and His righteousness
The treasures of earth and their glory
The favor of men and their praise

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says that when you seek God's kingdom first, all these things will be added unto you.

cards.text: Then Jesus wraps it up: do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Nobody clocks in for Friday's shift on a Monday, friend.

cards.question: Jesus says not to worry about tomorrow, because today has enough ___ of its own.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Today's batch is done, but trust me, friend, Jesus isn't finished teaching on that mountain.

findings.problem: The joke 'I went dull in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS' changes his backstory. In the backstory, he got worn down from years of baking before he went into the drawer. That wearing down is why he was put there. The drawer didn't dull him.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The flashlight joke ends by explaining itself: 'because the one thing that was supposed to light the way is dark too.' It is also one long run-on sentence held together by commas. That works against bite-sized cards.

The right answer 'money' is a thing, but the wrong answers 'Caesar' and 'Pharaoh' are people. The question also says 'after all that talk about treasure.' Together, these make the right answer stand out as the only answer of its kind.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question says 'all these things will be added unto you,' but it never says what 'these things' are. Food, drink and clothes were only named on earlier cards that are no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The line saying the teaching isn't over copies the doc's example: 'And that's where we'll leave it for now' and 'trust me, friend.' It should be a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Three cards use the same joke premise: years in the junk drawer (stop 1 card 3, stop 2 card 1, stop 2 card 6). Two of them are almost the same gag about worrying in the drawer for years (stop 2 cards 1 and 6). That weakens the second one.
findings.question: Should the docs limit how often one premise for a self-deprecating joke, like the junk drawer, can come back in a single lesson, or say that close repeats of the same gag should be avoided?
